claim: Use the review’s five-stage ladder to calibrate causal language.
context: Section 4 separates what each design contributes. Cross-sectional studies establish co-occurrence; longitudinal replication adds temporal ordering; genetic approaches provide genetically proxied estimates; controlled perturbations test mechanisms in a specified model; human interventions manipulate exposure in people. Microbiome MR depends on instrument strength, pleiotropy, ancestry and exposure definition; sensitivity analyses and convergence with other designs strengthen interpretation. The stages describe inference and triangulation rather than making every later-numbered design universally superior.
